inputs.code:
// Rule ids are stored under {items:[...]} because a bare array is dropped on write.
// The list returns COUNTS, not the ids - a page of 200 plans would otherwise carry
// 200 rule lists to render a table that shows neither.
def out = []
if (rows != null) rows.each { r ->
    def p = r.properties
    def cr = (p?.creditRules instanceof List) ? p.creditRules : []
    def pr = (p?.payoutRules instanceof List) ? p.payoutRules : []
    out << [planId: p?.planId ?: '', recordId: String.valueOf(r.id),
            name: p?.name ?: '', description: p?.description ?: '',
            periodId: p?.periodId ?: '', status: p?.status ?: '',
            version: p?.version, startDate: p?.startDate, endDate: p?.endDate,
            creditRuleCount: cr.size(), payoutRuleCount: pr.size()]
}
int tot = (total == null) ? out.size() : Integer.valueOf(String.valueOf(total))
return [plans: out, total: tot, hasMore: (pageOffset + out.size()) < tot,
        message: out.size() + ' plan' + (out.size() == 1 ? '' : 's') + ' on this page']
